repo.description:
An authenticated system user holding the **Owner** role (at root, namespace, or database level, scoped to the target database) can crash a SurrealDB server by uploading a small malformed `.surml` file to the `/ml/import` endpoint.

The uploaded bytes are passed directly into the SurrealML header parser, which used unchecked `unwrap()` calls and array indexing on attacker-controlled header fields. A malformed field - for example a non-numeric input-dimensions value - panics during header parsing. Because `surrealdb-core` is built with `panic = 'abort'`, the panic terminates the entire server process.

### Impact

What an attacker **can** do:

- With the **Owner** role (at root, namespace, or database level, scoped to the target database), crash the entire server with a single small malformed `.surml` upload to `/ml/import`.
- Deny service to every namespace and database on that instance until it is restarted - because `surrealdb-core` is built with `panic = 'abort'`, the panic aborts the whole process, not just the request.

What it **can't** do:

- Reach this code path without the Owner role - record/scope users and users holding only the Editor or Viewer role cannot call `/ml/import`.
- Affect confidentiality or integrity - the crash occurs during import parsing, before the model is stored (availability only).
- Affect deployments built without the `ml` feature, or that do not expose the `/ml/import` route.

### Patches

A patch has been introduced that makes the SurrealML header parsers fail closed: malformed input-dimensions, origin, and output/normaliser fields now return a structured `BadRequest` error instead of panicking, so a malformed upload is rejected with an error response rather than crashing the server.

- Versions 3.1.6 and later are not affected by this issue.

### Workarounds

Users unable to patch should consider the following workarounds:

- Build or deploy without the `ml` feature if machine-learning model import/export is not required.
- Grant the Owner role sparingly; only Owners can import models, so callers without it cannot reach the vulnerable code path.
- Run SurrealDB under a process supervisor that restarts it on exit (e.g. Kubernetes, systemd `Restart=on-failure`, or a Docker restart policy), so the server recovers immediately after a crash. This limits downtime but does not prevent the crash.

### References

- [DEFINE MODEL](https://surrealdb.com/docs/surrealql/statements/define/model)
- [SurrealDB Documentation - Capabilities](https://surrealdb.com/docs/surrealdb/security/capabilities)
- `fix(surrealml): reject malformed model headers instead of panicking` (included in SurrealDB 3.2.0 and backported to 3.1.6)
- [surrealdb/surrealml](https://github.com/surrealdb/surrealml) - the standalone `surrealml-core` crate carries the same parser; the fix must be mirrored there.
- [GHSA-wjjj-24cx-f28g](https://github.com/surrealdb/surrealdb/security/advisories/GHSA-wjjj-24cx-f28g) - related `panic = 'abort'` denial-of-service in RPC handling.

### Acknowledgements

Thank you to [sondt99](https://github.com/sondt99) for reporting this issue.
